title.zh: 卷46 竇瑾 許彦 李欣
title.en: Volume 46: Dou Jin, Xu Yan, Li Xin
title.raw: 卷46 竇瑾 許彦 李欣 Volume 46: Dou Jin, Xu Yan, Li Xin

sentences.zh: 竇瑾 許彥 李訢

translations.literal: Dou Jin; Xu Yan; Li Xin
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin; Xu Yan; Li Xin

sentences.zh: 竇瑾，字道瑜，頓丘衞國人也。

translations.literal: Dou Jin, courtesy name Daoyu, was a native of Dunqiu in Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin, whose courtesy name was Daoyu, came from Dunqiu in Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 自云漢司空融之後。

translations.literal: He claimed to be a descendant of Rong, Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Rong, who had served as Grand Commandant under the Han.

sentences.zh: 高祖成為頓丘太守，因家焉。

translations.literal: His ancestor Cheng became Administrator of Dunqiu under the High Ancestor, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: An ancestor named Cheng had served as Administrator of Dunqiu under the dynasty's High Ancestor, and the family made its home there.

sentences.zh: 瑾少以文學知名。

translations.literal: Jin was famed from youth for his literary accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: From his youth Jin was known for his learning and literary skill.

sentences.zh: 自中書博士，為中書侍郎，賜爵繁陽子，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: From Doctor of the Secretariat he became Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat, was granted the title Marquis of Fanyang, and was given the additional office of General for Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Doctor of the Secretariat to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang, and was given the additional rank of General for Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 參與軍國之謀，屢有軍功。

translations.literal: He took part in planning for state and army affairs and repeatedly earned military merit.
translations.idiomatic: He joined in counsel on affairs of state and army and won military distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書監，進爵衞國侯，加冠軍將軍，轉西部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, advanced to Marquis of Weiguo, given the additional rank of General Who Wins Victories, and moved to Senior Secretary of the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, raised to Marquis of Weiguo, given the additional title of General Who Wins Victories, and transferred to Senior Secretary of the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 初定三秦，人猶去就，拜使持節、散騎常侍、都督秦雍二州諸軍事、寧西將軍、長安鎮將、毗陵公。

translations.literal: When the Three Qins were first pacified and the people were still deciding whether to stay or go, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant, Supervisor of military affairs in Qin and Yong provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, Commander-in-Chief at Chang'an, and Duke of Piling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Qins had just been brought under control and the populace was still wavering in allegiance, he received appointment as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant, Supervisor of all military affairs in Qin and Yong provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, garrison commander at Chang'an, and Duke of Piling.

sentences.zh: 在鎮八年，甚著威惠。

translations.literal: He held the garrison post for eight years and became greatly renowned for authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at his post for eight years and won wide renown for both stern authority and generous kindness.

sentences.zh: 徵為殿中、都官尚書，仍散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as Director of the Palace and Director of the Bureau of Justice, while retaining his post as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Director of the Palace and Director of the Bureau of Justice, and kept his rank as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖親待之，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu treated him with personal favor and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu favored him personally and heaped lavish rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 從征蓋吳，先驅慰諭，因平巴西氐、羌酋領，降下數千家，不下者誅之。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Gai Wu, went ahead as vanguard to reassure and instruct, and thereby pacified Di and Qiang chieftains in Baxi; several thousand households submitted, and those who would not were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the expedition against Gai Wu, riding ahead as vanguard to offer reassurance and persuasion, and in the process subdued Di and Qiang leaders in Baxi. Several thousand households surrendered; those who refused were put to death.

sentences.zh: 又降蠻酋仇天爾等三千家於五將山。

translations.literal: He also induced the surrender at Mount Wujiang of three thousand households under the Man chieftain Chou Tian'er and others.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise brought about the submission at Mount Wujiang of three thousand households led by the Man chieftain Chou Tian'er and others.

sentences.zh: 蓋吳平，瑾留鎮長安。

translations.literal: When Gai Wu was pacified, Jin remained to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Gai Wu was defeated, Jin stayed behind to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 還京，復為殿中、都官，典左右執法。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he again served as Director of the Palace and Director of the Bureau of Justice, overseeing law enforcement on the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital he again held the posts of Director of the Palace and Director of the Bureau of Justice, with charge of judicial enforcement at court.

sentences.zh: 世祖歎曰：「古者右賢左戚，國之良翰，毗陵公之謂矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sighed and said, "In antiquity the worthy were placed on the right and kinsmen on the left—they were the state's firm pillars. This is what is meant by the Duke of Piling."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu exclaimed, "In ancient times the worthy stood to the right and kinsmen to the left—they were the state's true pillars. That is precisely what the Duke of Piling represents."

sentences.zh: 」恭宗薨於東宮，瑾兼司徒，奉詔冊諡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongzong died in the Eastern Palace, Jin concurrently held the post of Minister of Education and received the edict to confer the posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongzong died in the Eastern Palace, Jin served concurrently as Minister of Education and, by imperial command, drew up the posthumous designation.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮南將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General Who Guards the South and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as General Who Guards the South and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 清約沖素，憂勤王事，著稱當時。

translations.literal: Frugal, plain, and unadorned, he devoted himself anxiously to the king's affairs and won renown in his own day.
translations.idiomatic: Plain in living and unassuming in manner, he threw himself into the service of the throne and was widely praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 還為內都大官。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Grand Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Grand Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 興光初，瑾女壻鬱林公司馬彌陀以選尚臨涇公主，瑾教彌陀辭託，有誹謗呪詛之言，與彌陀同誅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xingguang era, Jin's son-in-law Moduo, a staff officer of the Prince of Yulin, was selected to marry Princess Linjing; Jin instructed Moduo to decline on pretext, and there were words of slander and curse; he was executed together with Moduo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingguang era, Jin's son-in-law Moduo, a staff officer attached to the Prince of Yulin, was chosen to marry Princess Linjing. Jin urged Moduo to refuse the match on one pretext or another, and words of slander and imprecation were involved; Jin was executed along with Moduo.

sentences.zh: 瑾有四子，秉、持、依並為中書學生，與父同時伏法。

translations.literal: Jin had four sons; Bing, Chi, and Yi were all students of the Secretariat, and suffered execution together with their father.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had four sons. Bing, Chi, and Yi were all students at the Secretariat school and were executed at the same time as their father.

sentences.zh: 唯少子遵，逃匿得免。

translations.literal: Only the youngest son Zun, by fleeing and hiding, escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Only the youngest son, Zun, escaped by going into hiding.

sentences.zh: 遵善楷篆，北京諸碑及臺殿樓觀、宮門題署，多遵書也。

translations.literal: Zun excelled in regular and seal script; on steles throughout the northern capital, and on inscriptions for terraces, halls, towers, pavilions, and palace gates, most were in Zun's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was skilled in regular and seal script. Most of the steles in the northern capital and the inscriptions on palace terraces, halls, towers, and gates were written by him.

sentences.zh: 官至尚書郎、濮陽太守，多所受納。

translations.literal: He rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Puyang, and accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the posts of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and Administrator of Puyang, and took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 其子僧演，姦通民婦，為民賈邈所告，免官。

translations.literal: His son Sengyan committed adultery with a commoner's wife; he was denounced by the commoner Jia Miao and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengyan had an affair with a commoner's wife; a man named Jia Miao reported him, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 後以善書，拜庫部令，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, for his skill in calligraphy, he was appointed Director of the Storehouse Bureau and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of his calligraphy, he was appointed Director of the Storehouse Bureau and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 許彥，字道謨，小字嘉屯，高陽新城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Yan, courtesy name Daomo, childhood name Jiatun, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan, whose courtesy name was Daomo and childhood name Jiatun, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，慕容氏高陽太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was Administrator of Gaoyang under the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao had served as Administrator of Gaoyang under the Murong.

sentences.zh: 彥少孤貧，好讀書，後從沙門法叡受易。

translations.literal: Yan was orphaned and poor in youth, loved reading, and later studied the Changes under the monk Farui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan lost his parents early and grew up in poverty, but he loved books and later studied the Book of Changes under the monk Farui.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，被徵，以卜筮頻驗，遂在左右，參與謀議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizu's reign he was summoned; because his divination and casting proved repeatedly accurate, he remained at the emperor's side and took part in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizu's reign he was summoned to court. His divinations proved accurate time after time, so he stayed at the emperor's side and joined in deliberations.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎常侍，賜爵博陵侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant and granted the title Marquis of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Boling.

sentences.zh: 彥質厚慎密，與人言不及內事。

translations.literal: Yan was sincere, thick, and cautious; in conversation with others he never touched on inner-court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was steady, discreet, and trustworthy; in speaking with others he never mentioned affairs of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 世祖以此益親待之。

translations.literal: For this reason Emperor Shizu treated him with still greater personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued this discretion and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 進爵武昌公，拜安東將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Wuchang and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Wuchang and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州受納，多違法度，詔書切讓之。

translations.literal: While in the province he accepted bribes and often violated the law; an edict sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: In his province he took bribes and frequently broke the law; the throne sent him a sharply worded rebuke.

sentences.zh: 然以彥腹心近臣，弗之罪也。

translations.literal: Yet because Yan was a trusted intimate, he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan was a trusted confidant, however, he went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 真君二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenjun he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Duke Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子宗之，初入為中散，領內祕書。

translations.literal: His son Zongzhi, on first entering service, became Palace Scribe and headed the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongzhi entered service as Palace Scribe and headed the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖臨江，賜爵高鄉侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu crossed the Yangzi, he was granted the title Marquis of Gaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu campaigned on the Yangzi, Zongzhi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 高宗踐阼，遷殿中尚書，出為鎮東將軍、定州刺史，潁川公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing in the Palace, then sent out as General Who Guards the East and Governor of Dingzhou, and made Duke of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Zongzhi was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing in the Palace, then sent out as General Who Guards the East and Governor of Dingzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 受敕討丁零，丁零既平，宗之因循郡縣，求取不節。

translations.literal: He received orders to campaign against the Dingling; after the Dingling were pacified, Zongzhi lingered in the commanderies and counties and extorted without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to campaign against the Dingling, he lingered in the districts after their defeat and extorted the people without restraint.

sentences.zh: 深澤人馬超毀謗宗之，宗之怒，遂毆殺超。

translations.literal: Ma Chao of Shenze slandered Zongzhi; Zongzhi grew angry and beat Chao to death.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Shenze named Ma Chao spoke ill of Zongzhi; enraged, Zongzhi beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 懼超家人告狀，上超謗訕朝政。

translations.literal: Fearing that Chao's family would bring suit, he reported that Chao had slandered the court and government.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Chao's kin would bring charges, he accused Chao of slandering the court and the government.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞之，曰：「此必妄也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong heard of it, he said, "This must be false."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong heard of it, he said, "This must be a fabrication."

sentences.zh: 朕為天下主，何惡於超，而超有此言。

translations.literal: "I am lord of all under Heaven—what wrong have I done Chao that he should speak thus?"
translations.idiomatic: "I am sovereign of the realm—what injury have I done Chao that he would say such things?"

sentences.zh: 必是宗之懼罪誣超。

translations.literal: "Surely Zongzhi, fearing punishment, has framed Chao."
translations.idiomatic: "Zongzhi must have invented the charge out of fear of punishment."

sentences.zh: 」按驗果然。

translations.literal: Investigation proved it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation confirmed that this was exactly what had happened.

sentences.zh: 事下有司，司空伊馛等以宗之腹心近臣，出居方伯，不能宣揚本朝，盡心綏導，而侵損齊民，枉殺良善，妄列無辜，上塵朝廷，誣詐不道，理合極刑。

translations.literal: The case was referred to the relevant offices; Minister of Works Yi Ba and others held that Zongzhi, as a trusted intimate, sent out to hold a regional command, had failed to proclaim and spread the court's policies or to guide and pacify with full devotion, but instead harmed the common people, wrongly killed the innocent, falsely charged the guiltless, and brought disgrace upon the court—deceit and outrage against the Way deserving the utmost penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was handed to the judicial offices. Minister of Works Yi Ba and others argued that Zongzhi, though a trusted confidant sent out as a regional commander, had failed to proclaim the court's policies or to govern the people with care. Instead he had preyed on the populace, killed an innocent man, and falsely accused the blameless, thereby shaming the throne through deceit and outrage deserving of the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 太安二年冬，遂斬於都南。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Taian he was beheaded south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Taian he was beheaded just south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宗之孫亮，字元規。

translations.literal: Zongzhi's grandson Liang, courtesy name Yuangui.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi's grandson Liang, whose courtesy name was Yuangui.

sentences.zh: 正光中，盪寇將軍，稍遷冀州驃騎長史、司徒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: During Zhengguang he was General Who Quells Bandits, and was gradually transferred to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry in Jizhou and Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he served as General Who Quells Bandits and was gradually promoted to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry in Jizhou and Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 年五十二，卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 宗之長兄熙，字德融，襲爵武昌公。

translations.literal: Zongzhi's elder brother Xi, courtesy name Derong, inherited the title Duke of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi's elder brother Xi, whose courtesy name was Derong, inherited the title of Duke of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 中書郎，早卒。

translations.literal: He was a Gentleman of the Secretariat and died young.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and died young.

sentences.zh: 子安仁，襲。

translations.literal: His son Anren inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anren inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除中書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安東將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 子元康，襲爵，後降為侯。

translations.literal: His son Yuankang inherited the title, which was later reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuankang inherited the title, which was later reduced from duke to marquis.

sentences.zh: 拜冠軍將軍、長安鎮副將。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Wins Victories and Deputy Commander of the Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Wins Victories and deputy commander of the Chang'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 遷監河州諸軍事、河州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of military affairs in Hezhou and Governor of Hezhou, retaining his general's rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervisor of military affairs in Hezhou and Governor of Hezhou, while keeping his rank as general.

sentences.zh: 入為廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: He entered court service as Vice Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Vice Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 除魏郡太守，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Weijun but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of Administrator of Weijun but firmly declined it.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈征虜將軍、營州刺史，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; posthumously he was given General Who Campaigns against the Barbarians and Governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously honored as General Who Campaigns against the Barbarians and Governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Su.

sentences.zh: 子廓，字崇遠，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Kuo, courtesy name Chongyuan, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuo, whose courtesy name was Chongyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，累遷頓丘、東太原二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and was successively transferred to serve as Administrator of Dunqiu and of Eastern Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and rose in turn to administer Dunqiu and Eastern Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，年二十八。

translations.literal: He died at the age of twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子子躬襲。

translations.literal: His son Zigong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zigong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 子躬，武定末，中外府水曹參軍。

translations.literal: Zigong, at the end of Wuding, was an aide in the Water Bureau of the Central and Outer Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong, late in the Wuding era, served as an aide in the Water Bureau of the Central and Outer Offices.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi dynasty accepted the abdication, his noble rank was reduced in the usual way.

sentences.zh: 子躬弟子憲，太尉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Zigong's younger brother's son Xian was an aide in the Central Troops Bureau under the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong's nephew Xian served as an aide in the Central Troops Bureau under the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 元康弟護，州主簿。

translations.literal: Yuankang's younger brother Hu was Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang's younger brother Hu served as Chief Clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 子瑞，字徵之，亦州主簿。

translations.literal: His son Rui, courtesy name Zhengzhi, also served as Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui, whose courtesy name was Zhengzhi, likewise served as Chief Clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 瑞弟絢，字伯禮，頗有業尚。

translations.literal: Rui's younger brother Xuan, courtesy name Boli, had considerable learning and moral purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's younger brother Xuan, whose courtesy name was Boli, was a man of learning and high principle.

sentences.zh: 閨門雍睦，三世同居。

translations.literal: His household was harmonious; three generations lived together.
translations.idiomatic: His household was harmonious, with three generations living under one roof.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書李神儁常稱其家風。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, often praised the family's moral tone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, often praised the family's conduct.

sentences.zh: 自侍御史累遷尚書左民郎、司徒諮議參軍，修起居注。

translations.literal: From Attending Censor he was successively promoted to Gentleman of the Left Bureau for the People in the Masters of Writing and Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education, and compiled the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as Attending Censor, he rose to Gentleman of the Left Bureau for the People in the Masters of Writing and Consulting Aide to the Minister of Education, and helped compile the court diary.

sentences.zh: 後拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 興和初卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Xinghe, at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xinghe era, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、都督冀瀛二州諸軍事、征東將軍、吏部尚書、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of military affairs in Ji and Ying provinces, General Who Campaigns East, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of military affairs in Ji and Ying provinces, General Who Campaigns East, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 絢弟遜，武定末，東陽平太守。

translations.literal: Xuan's younger brother Xun, at the end of Wuding, was Administrator of Eastern Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's younger brother Xun, late in the Wuding era, served as Administrator of Eastern Yangping.

sentences.zh: 遜弟曄，字叔明，性開率。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Ye, courtesy name Shuming, was by nature open and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Ye, whose courtesy name was Shuming, was open and forthright by nature.

sentences.zh: 州治中、別駕、西高陽太守、太中大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Clerk of the province, Administrator-in-Attendance, Administrator of Western Gaoyang, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Chief Clerk of the province, Administrator-in-Attendance, Administrator of Western Gaoyang, and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 興和三年卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Xinghe, at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Xinghe era, at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮東將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Guards the East and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Guards the East and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 曄弟惇，字季良。

translations.literal: Ye's younger brother Dun, courtesy name Jiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's younger brother Dun, whose courtesy name was Jiliang.

sentences.zh: 武定末，兼大司農卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he concurrently held the post of Minister of the National Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wuding era he served concurrently as Minister of the National Granaries.

sentences.zh: 熙弟龍，官至趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Long rose to Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Long rose to serve as Administrator of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫琰，字長琳，有幹用。

translations.literal: Sun Yan, courtesy name Changlin, was capable and effective.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yan, whose courtesy name was Changlin, was capable and effective in office.

sentences.zh: 初除太學博士，累遷尚書南主客郎、瀛州中正。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy and was successively promoted to Gentleman of the Southern Bureau for Guests in the Masters of Writing and Rectifier of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and rose in turn to Gentleman of the Southern Bureau for Guests in the Masters of Writing and Rectifier of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died during Xiaochang, at the age of forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xiaochang era, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，重贈散騎常侍、衞將軍、尚書右僕射、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he was again posthumously given Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, Vice Director of the Right in the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he received a further posthumous honor as Regular Attendant, General of the Guard, Vice Director of the Right in the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 琰弟璣，字仲衡，有識尚。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Ji, courtesy name Zhongheng, had discernment and high purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Ji, whose courtesy name was Zhongheng, was a man of insight and principle.

sentences.zh: 廣平王常侍、員外散騎侍郎、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Prince of Guangping, Extraordinary Attendant of the Secretariat, and Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Prince of Guangping, Extraordinary Attendant of the Secretariat, and Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 遷通直散騎常侍、瀛州大中正、散騎常侍、滎陽太守、行南青州事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant Direct and Upright, Senior Rectifier of Yingzhou, Regular Attendant, Administrator of Xingyang, and Acting Supervisor of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant Direct and Upright, Senior Rectifier of Yingzhou, Regular Attendant, Administrator of Xingyang, and acting supervisor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 琰兄弟並通率，多與勝流交遊。

translations.literal: Yan and his brothers were all open and forthright, and associated much with leading men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his brothers were all open and unpretentious, and they moved in the circles of the day's leading scholars and gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 又有博陵許赤虎，涉獵經史，善嘲謔。

translations.literal: There was also Xu Chihu of Boling, who ranged through the classics and histories and excelled at banter and jest.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Xu Chihu of Boling, a man who had read widely in the classics and histories and was skilled at witty banter.

sentences.zh: 延興中，著作佐郎，與慕容白曜南討。

translations.literal: During Yanxing he was Assistant Gentleman of Composition and joined Murong Baiyao on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era he served as Assistant Gentleman of Composition and accompanied Murong Baiyao on the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 後使江南，應對敏捷，雖言不典故，而南人頗稱機辯滑稽焉。

translations.literal: Later he was sent to the south of the Yangzi; his replies were quick, and though his speech was not laden with classical allusion, southerners praised his wit and humor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent on a mission south of the Yangzi. His replies were quick and sharp; though he did not speak in learned allusions, southerners praised him for his wit and humor.

sentences.zh: 使還，為東郡太守，卒官。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he became Administrator of Dongjun and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from his mission he was appointed Administrator of Dongjun and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 子陀，定州長史。

translations.literal: His son Tuo was Chief Clerk of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuo served as Chief Clerk of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 李訢，字元盛，小名真奴，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Xin, courtesy name Yuansheng, childhood name Zhennu, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin, whose courtesy name was Yuansheng and childhood name Zhennu, came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾袓產，產子績，二世知名於慕容氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chan and Chan's son Ji were both famed for two generations under the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chan and Chan's son Ji had both won renown for two generations under the Murong.

sentences.zh: 父崇，馮跋吏部尚書、石城太守。

translations.literal: His father Chong was Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Shicheng under Feng Ba.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong had served Feng Ba as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Administrator of Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 延和初，車駕至和龍，崇率十餘郡歸降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanhe the imperial carriage reached Helong; Chong led more than ten commanderies in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanhe era, when the emperor reached Helong, Chong led more than ten commanderies in submitting to the Wei court.

sentences.zh: 世袓甚禮之，呼曰「李公」，以崇為平西將軍、北幽州刺史、固安侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu treated him with great courtesy, calling him "Lord Li," and appointed Chong General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Northern Youzhou, and Marquis of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu honored him greatly, addressing him as "Lord Li," and appointed him General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Northern Youzhou, and Marquis of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一，諡曰襄侯。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one; his posthumous title was Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one and was given the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 訢母賤，為諸兄所輕。

translations.literal: Xin's mother was of low status, and he was slighted by his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xin's mother was of humble birth, his elder brothers looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 崇曰：「此子之生，相者言貴，吾每觀察，或未可知。

translations.literal: Chong said, "When this son was born, the physiognomist said he would be noble; each time I observe him, it may yet prove true."
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "When this boy was born, a physiognomist declared he would rise to greatness. Each time I watch him, I think that may yet come true."

sentences.zh: 」遂使入都，為中書學生。

translations.literal: He therefore sent him to the capital to become a student of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly sent the boy to the capital to enroll as a student at the Secretariat school.

sentences.zh: 世袓幸中書學，見而異之，指謂從者曰：「此小兒終效用於朕之子孫矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu visited the Secretariat school, he saw Xin and was struck by him; pointing, he said to his attendants, "This boy will in the end prove useful to my sons and grandsons."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu visited the Secretariat school, he noticed Xin and was impressed. Pointing at him, he told his attendants, "This boy will one day serve my sons and grandsons well."

sentences.zh: 」因識眄之。

translations.literal: He thereby took note of him with a favorable glance.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the emperor marked him for favor.

sentences.zh: 世袓舅陽平王杜超有女，將許貴戚。

translations.literal: Du Chao, Prince of Yangping and the emperor's maternal uncle, had a daughter who was to be betrothed to a noble house.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chao, Prince of Yangping and the emperor's uncle by marriage, had a daughter who was about to be betrothed to a noble family.

sentences.zh: 世袓聞之，謂超曰：「李訢後必宦達，益人門戶，可以女妻之，勿許他貴也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu heard of it, he told Chao, "Li Xin will surely rise to high office hereafter and bring honor to any household; you may give him your daughter in marriage—do not betroth her to another noble."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he told Chao, "Li Xin is bound for high office and will bring honor to whatever house he joins. Give him your daughter in marriage, and do not promise her to another noble family."

sentences.zh: 」遂勸成婚。

translations.literal: He thereupon urged that the marriage be concluded.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed for the marriage to be concluded.

sentences.zh: 南人李哲嘗言訢必當貴達。

translations.literal: The southerner Li Zhe had once said that Xin would surely rise to wealth and high rank.
translations.idiomatic: A southerner named Li Zhe had once predicted that Xin would rise to wealth and high office.

sentences.zh: 杜超之死也，世袓親哭三日。

translations.literal: When Du Chao died, Emperor Shizu personally mourned him for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chao died, Emperor Shizu personally mourned him for three days.

sentences.zh: 訢以超壻，得在喪位出入。

translations.literal: Because Xin was Chao's son-in-law, he was allowed to come and go at the mourning site.
translations.idiomatic: As Chao's son-in-law, Xin was permitted to come and go at the mourning site.

sentences.zh: 帝目而指之，謂左右曰：「觀此人舉動，豈不有異於眾？

translations.literal: The emperor fixed his gaze on him and pointed, saying to those beside him, "Look at this man's bearing—is it not unlike that of others?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fixed his eyes on him and said to those around him, "Look at this man's bearing—is it not unlike that of ordinary men?"

sentences.zh: 必為朕家幹事之臣。

translations.literal: "He will surely become a minister who accomplishes great deeds for my house."
translations.idiomatic: "He is sure to become a minister who will accomplish great deeds for my house."

sentences.zh: 」訢聰敏機辯，強記明察。

translations.literal: Xin was clever, quick, and resourceful in debate, with a strong memory and keen perception.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was clever, quick-witted, and sharp in debate, with a formidable memory and keen powers of observation.

sentences.zh: 初，李靈為高宗博士、諮議，[1]詔崔浩選中書學生器業優者為助教。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Ling had been Erudite and Consulting Aide to Emperor Gaozong; an edict ordered Cui Hao to select students of the Secretariat school whose talent and learning were outstanding to serve as assistant teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Ling had served Emperor Gaozong as Erudite and Consulting Aide. An edict ordered Cui Hao to choose the most capable students at the Secretariat school to serve as assistant teachers.

sentences.zh: 浩舉其弟子箱子與盧度世、李敷三人應之。

translations.literal: Hao nominated his disciple Xiangzi together with Lu Dushi and Li Fu, three men, to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Hao nominated his own disciple Xiangzi, together with Lu Dushi and Li Fu, for the appointments.

sentences.zh: 給事高讜子祐、尚書段霸兒姪等以為浩阿其親戚，言於恭宗。

translations.literal: Gao You, son of the Attendant Gao Dan, and Duan Ba's nephew and others held that Hao was favoring his kinsmen, and spoke of it to Emperor Gongzong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao You, son of the Attendant Gao Dan, and a nephew of Duan Ba, among others, believed that Hao was favoring his own kin and reported this to Emperor Gongzong.

sentences.zh: 恭宗以浩為不平，聞之於世袓。

translations.literal: Emperor Gongzong, deeming Hao unfair, reported it to Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gongzong, judging Hao's conduct unfair, reported the matter to Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 世袓意在於訢，曰：「云何不取幽州刺史李崇老翁兒也？

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu's intent was on Xin; he said, "Why not take the old man Li Chong's son, the former Governor of Youzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu's mind was set on Xin. He said, "Why not choose the son of old Li Chong, the former Governor of Youzhou?"

sentences.zh: 」浩對曰：「前亦言訢合選，但以其先行在外，故不取之。

translations.literal: Hao replied, "I too said earlier that Xin was fit for selection, but because he had already gone abroad I did not choose him."
translations.idiomatic: Hao replied, "I had said earlier that Xin was qualified, but because he was already away on assignment I did not name him."

sentences.zh: 」世袓曰：「可待訢還，箱子等罷之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu said, "We may wait until Xin returns, and then dismiss Xiangzi and the others."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We can wait until Xin returns, and then dismiss Xiangzi and the others."

sentences.zh: 」訢為世袓所識如此。

translations.literal: Thus was Xin marked out by Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Xin came to be singled out by Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 遂除中書助教博士，稍見任用，入授高宗經。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Assistant Teacher and Erudite of the Secretariat, was gradually employed, and entered the palace to instruct Emperor Gaozong in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Teacher and Erudite of the Secretariat, was gradually given greater responsibility, and entered the palace to instruct the crown prince in the classics.

sentences.zh: 訢上疏求立學校曰：「臣聞至治之隆，非文德無以經綸王道；

translations.literal: Xin submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of schools, saying, "Your servant has heard that the height of supreme governance cannot weave the kingly Way without civil virtue;"
translations.idiomatic: Xin submitted a memorial asking that schools be established, saying, "I have heard that the height of perfect governance cannot sustain the kingly Way without civil virtue;"

sentences.zh: 太平之美，非良才無以光贊皇化。

translations.literal: "the beauty of great peace cannot glorify and support the imperial transformation without excellent talent."
translations.idiomatic: "and the splendor of an age of great peace cannot glorify and advance the imperial transformation without men of outstanding talent."

sentences.zh: 是以昔之明主，建庠序於京畿，立學官於郡邑，教國子弟，習其道藝。

translations.literal: "Therefore enlightened rulers of old built academies in the capital region, established school officials in commanderies and districts, taught the sons of the state, and had them study the Way and its arts."
translations.idiomatic: "For this reason enlightened rulers of old built academies in the capital region, established school officials in every commandery and district, taught the sons of the state, and had them study the Way and its arts."

sentences.zh: 然後選其俊異，以為造士。

translations.literal: "Only then did they select the outstanding among them to become accomplished scholars."
translations.idiomatic: "Only then did they select the most outstanding among them to become accomplished scholars for the state."

sentences.zh: 今聖治欽明，道隆三五，九服之民，咸仰德化，而所在州土，學校未立。

translations.literal: "Now the sage governance is revered and bright, the Way surpasses that of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and the people of the nine domains all look up to the imperial transformation—yet in the provinces and lands where I serve, schools have not been established."
translations.idiomatic: "Today Your Majesty's sage rule is revered and bright, your Way surpasses that of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and the people of the nine domains all look up to your transforming virtue—yet in the provinces where I serve, no schools have yet been established."

sentences.zh: 臣雖不敏，誠願備之，使後生聞雅頌之音，童幼覩經教之本。

translations.literal: "Though your servant is not clever, he sincerely wishes to provide for this, so that later generations may hear the music of the Odes and Hymns and children may behold the roots of classical teaching."
translations.idiomatic: "Though I am not clever, I sincerely wish to provide for this, so that later generations may hear the music of the Odes and Hymns and children may behold the foundations of classical teaching."

sentences.zh: 臣昔蒙恩寵，長管中祕，時課修學有成立之人，髦俊之士，已蒙進用。

translations.literal: "Your servant once received favor and long directed the Inner Secretariat; at that time those who studied and achieved completion, and the outstanding talents, were already advanced and employed."
translations.idiomatic: "I was once favored and long directed the Inner Secretariat. Students who completed their studies and outstanding talents from that time have already been promoted and employed."

sentences.zh: 臣今重荷榮遇，顯任方岳，思闡帝猷，光宣於外。

translations.literal: "Your servant now again bears honored appointment in a prominent post as a regional commander, and wishes to unfold the emperor's designs and spread their radiance abroad."
translations.idiomatic: "I now bear honored appointment again as a regional commander, and I wish to unfold Your Majesty's designs and spread their radiance throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 自到以來，訪諸文學，舊德已老，後生未進。

translations.literal: "Since arriving I have inquired among men of letters: the old worthies have grown aged, and the younger generation has not advanced."
translations.idiomatic: "Since my arrival I have sought out men of learning: the old masters have grown aged, and the younger generation has not yet advanced."

sentences.zh: 歲首所貢，雖依制遣，對問之日，懼不克堪。

translations.literal: "Those presented at the year's beginning, though sent according to regulation, on the day of examination I fear they will not measure up."
translations.idiomatic: "The candidates presented at the year's beginning are sent according to regulation, but on the day of examination I fear they will not measure up."

sentences.zh: 臣愚欲仰依先典，於州郡治所各立學官。

translations.literal: "Your servant, in his folly, wishes to follow the ancient canon and establish school officials at each provincial and commandery seat."
translations.idiomatic: "In my folly I wish to follow the ancient canon and establish school officials at each provincial and commandery seat."

sentences.zh: 使士望之流、冠冕之胄，就而受業，庶必有成。

translations.literal: "Let men of local standing and heirs of eminent houses come to receive instruction—perhaps they will surely achieve success."
translations.idiomatic: "Let men of local standing and heirs of eminent houses come to receive instruction there, and perhaps they will achieve real success."

sentences.zh: 其經藝通明者貢之王府。

translations.literal: "Those whose mastery of the classics is clear and thorough should be presented to the imperial court."
translations.idiomatic: "Those whose mastery of the classics is thorough should be presented to the imperial court."

sentences.zh: 則郁郁之文，於是不墜。

translations.literal: "Then the flourishing of culture will thereby not fall away."
translations.idiomatic: "Then the flourishing of culture will not be lost."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，顯袓從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xianzu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Xianzu approved it.

sentences.zh: 以訢治為諸州之最，加賜衣服。

translations.literal: Because Xin's governance ranked first among all provinces, he was additionally granted robes.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xin's governance ranked first among all the provinces, he received an additional gift of robes.

sentences.zh: 自是遂有驕矜自得之志。

translations.literal: From this time he came to harbor pride and self-satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on he grew proud and self-satisfied.

sentences.zh: 乃受納民財及商胡珍寶。

translations.literal: He then accepted the people's wealth and precious goods from merchant foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: He then accepted bribes from the people and precious goods from foreign merchants.

sentences.zh: 兵民告言，尚書李敷與訢少長相好，每左右之。

translations.literal: Soldiers and commoners reported it; Li Fu of the Masters of Writing had been on friendly terms with Xin since youth and always sided with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and commoners reported the matter. Li Fu of the Masters of Writing had been close to Xin since they were young and always spoke in his favor.

sentences.zh: 或有勸以奏聞，敷不許。

translations.literal: Some urged that it be reported to the throne, but Fu would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that the matter be reported to the throne, but Fu would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 顯袓聞訢罪狀，檻車徵訢，拷劾抵罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzu heard of Xin's crimes, he summoned Xin in a caged cart and interrogated him under torture until guilt was established.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu learned of Xin's crimes, he had Xin brought to court in a prisoner cart and interrogated under torture until his guilt was established.

sentences.zh: 時敷兄弟將見疏斥，有司諷訢以中旨嫌敷兄弟之意，令訢告列敷等隱罪，可得自全。

translations.literal: At that time the Fu brothers were about to be cast aside; the relevant offices hinted to Xin that the emperor inwardly resented the Fu brothers, and that if Xin reported and listed their hidden crimes he could preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Fu brothers were about to fall from favor. The judicial offices hinted to Xin that the emperor secretly resented them and that if Xin reported their hidden crimes he could save himself.

sentences.zh: 訢深所不欲，且弗之知也。

translations.literal: Xin deeply did not wish this and moreover did not know of their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was deeply unwilling to do this and, moreover, knew nothing of their crimes.

sentences.zh: 乃謂其女壻裴攸曰：「吾宗與李敷族世雖遠，情如一家。

translations.literal: He then said to his son-in-law Pei You, "My clan and the Li Fu clan, though distant in generations, are as close as one family in feeling."
translations.idiomatic: He then said to his son-in-law Pei You, "My clan and the Li Fu clan are distant in lineage, but in feeling we are like one family."

sentences.zh: 在事既有此勸，竟如何也？

translations.literal: "In this affair there is already such urging—what is finally to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: "In this affair I have already been urged to act—what am I finally to do?"

sentences.zh: 昨來每欲為此取死，引簪自刺，以帶自絞，而不能致絕。

translations.literal: "Yesterday I several times wished to die for this cause, drawing a hairpin to stab myself and using a belt to strangle myself, yet could not bring about my end."
translations.idiomatic: "Yesterday I several times wished to die rather than do this—I drew a hairpin to stab myself and used my belt to strangle myself, yet I could not bring about my end."

sentences.zh: 且亦不知其事。

translations.literal: "Moreover, I do not even know of the matter."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, I do not even know what crimes they are supposed to have committed."

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「何為為他死也？

translations.literal: You said, "Why die for another?"
translations.idiomatic: You replied, "Why should you die for them?"

sentences.zh: 敷兄弟事釁可知。

translations.literal: "The Fu brothers' offenses are clear."
translations.idiomatic: "The Fu brothers' offenses are plain enough."

sentences.zh: 有馮闡者，先為敷所敗，其家切恨之，但呼闡弟問之，足知委曲。

translations.literal: "There is one Feng Kan, whom Fu had earlier ruined; his family bitterly hates him. Simply summon Kan's younger brother and question him—you will fully know the details."
translations.idiomatic: "There is a man named Feng Kan whom Fu ruined earlier; his family hates Fu bitterly. Simply summon Kan's younger brother and question him, and you will learn the full story."

sentences.zh: 」訢從其言。

translations.literal: Xin followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xin followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 又趙郡范𢷋具條列敷兄弟事狀，有司以聞。

translations.literal: Fan Xie of Zhao Commandery also set forth in full detail the circumstances of the Fu brothers' affairs, and the relevant offices reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xie of Zhao Commandery also drew up a detailed account of the Fu brothers' offenses, and the judicial offices reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 敷坐得罪。

translations.literal: Fu was convicted of crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was found guilty and punished.

sentences.zh: 詔列訢貪冒，罪應死。

translations.literal: An edict listed Xin's greed and corruption; his crime deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict listed Xin's greed and corruption; his crime deserved death.

sentences.zh: 以糾李敷兄弟，故得降免，百鞭髠刑，配為厮役。

translations.literal: Because he had exposed the Li Fu brothers, he was granted reduction of sentence: a hundred lashes, shaving as punishment, and assignment as a menial servant.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had exposed the Li Fu brothers, his sentence was reduced to a hundred lashes, shaving of the head, and assignment as a menial servant.

sentences.zh: 訢之廢也，平壽侯張讜見訢，與語奇之，謂人曰：「此佳士也，終不久屈。

translations.literal: When Xin was disgraced, Zhang Chan, Marquis of Pingshou, saw Xin and, speaking with him, found him remarkable; he told others, "This is an excellent man; he will not long remain in humiliation."
translations.idiomatic: When Xin fell from favor, Zhang Chan, Marquis of Pingshou, met him and was struck by him in conversation. He told others, "This is an excellent man; he will not remain humbled for long."

sentences.zh: 」未幾而復為太倉尚書，攝南部事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Director of the Grand Granary and took charge of southern-bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed Director of the Grand Granary and put in charge of southern-bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 用范𢷋、陳端等計，令千里之外，戶別轉運，詣倉輸之。

translations.literal: Adopting the plans of Fan Xie, Chen Duan, and others, he ordered that a thousand li away each household should transport separately and deliver grain to the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Following the plans of Fan Xie, Chen Duan, and others, he ordered households a thousand li away to transport grain separately and deliver it to the granaries.

sentences.zh: 所在委滯，停延歲月，百姓競以貨賂各求在前，於是遠近大為困弊。

translations.literal: Everywhere goods piled up and stalled, delays stretched for months, and the common people vied in bribes to secure priority—thus near and far were greatly impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere grain piled up and stalled, delays stretched for months, and common people vied in bribes to move ahead in line. Near and far alike were plunged into hardship.

sentences.zh: 道路羣議曰：「畜聚斂之臣，未若盜臣。

translations.literal: Public talk along the roads said, "Keeping a minister who amasses wealth is not as good as keeping a thief."
translations.idiomatic: People along the roads said, "A minister who amasses wealth is worse than a thief."

sentences.zh: 」訢弟左將軍璞謂訢曰：「范𢷋善能降人以色，假人以辭，未聞德義之言，但有勢利之說。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Pu, General of the Left, said to Xin, "Fan Xie is skilled at winning men with pleasing looks and lending them fine words; one never hears talk of virtue and righteousness—only words of power and profit."
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Pu, General of the Left, said to him, "Fan Xie is skilled at winning men with a pleasant manner and lending them fine phrases. You never hear him speak of virtue and righteousness—only of power and profit."

sentences.zh: 聽其言也甘，察其行也賊，所謂諂諛、讒慝、貪冒、姦佞，不早絕之，後悔無及。

translations.literal: "His words sound sweet, but examine his conduct and it is treacherous—the sort called flatterer, slanderer, greedy, and villainous. If you do not cut him off early, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: "His words sound sweet, but look at his conduct and it is treacherous—the very type called flatterer, slanderer, greedy, and villainous. If you do not cut him off now, you will regret it when it is too late."

sentences.zh: 」訢不從，彌信之，腹心之事，皆以告𢷋。

translations.literal: Xin did not follow this advice but trusted Fan Xie all the more, telling him everything that lay closest to his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xin would not listen. He trusted Fan Xie all the more and confided in him every matter closest to his heart.

sentences.zh: 訢既寵於顯袓，參決軍國大議，兼典選舉，權傾內外，百僚莫不曲節以事之。

translations.literal: Once Xin was favored by Emperor Xianzu, he took part in deciding great affairs of state and army, also directed selections for office, and his power tilted inside and outside the court; no official failed to bend the knee in serving him.
translations.idiomatic: Once favored by Emperor Xianzu, Xin joined in deciding the great affairs of state and army, also controlled appointments, and his power dominated court and realm alike. No official failed to bow and scrape in serving him.

sentences.zh: 𢷋以無功，起家拜慮奴令。

translations.literal: Fan Xie, though without merit, began his career with appointment as Magistrate of Lunu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xie, though he had done nothing to deserve it, began his official career as Magistrate of Lunu.

sentences.zh: 延興末，詔曰：「尚書李訢著勳先朝，弼諧皇極，讜言嘉謀，旬日屢進，實國家之楨幹，當今之老成也。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanxing an edict said, "Li Xin of the Masters of Writing rendered distinguished service in the former court, assisted and harmonized the imperial apex, and within ten days repeatedly offered forthright words and excellent plans—truly a pillar of the state and a seasoned elder of the present age."
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Yanxing era an edict declared, "Li Xin of the Masters of Writing rendered distinguished service under the previous emperor, assisted the throne, and within ten days repeatedly offered forthright counsel and excellent plans. He is truly a pillar of the state and a seasoned elder of our own day."

sentences.zh: 是以擢授南部，綜理煩務。

translations.literal: "Therefore he is promoted to the southern bureau to oversee troublesome affairs in full."
translations.idiomatic: "For this reason he is promoted to the southern bureau to oversee its most burdensome affairs."

sentences.zh: 自在厥位，夙夜惟夤，乃心匪懈，克己復禮，退食自公，利上之事，知無不為，賞罰所加，不避疏戚。

translations.literal: "Since taking this post he has toiled early and late without slackening his heart, restrained himself and returned to ritual, left office meals with public duty in mind, and in matters benefiting the sovereign has known nothing he would not do; in rewards and punishments he has not spared kin near or distant."
translations.idiomatic: "Since taking this post he has labored early and late without slackening, restrained himself and returned to propriety, left his meals with public duty in mind, and in all matters benefiting the throne has done whatever needed doing. In rewards and punishments he has not spared kin near or distant."

sentences.zh: 雖孝子之思慈母，鷹鸇之逐鳥雀，何以方之。

translations.literal: "Even a filial son's longing for a loving mother, or a hawk's pursuit of sparrows—how could these serve as comparison?"
translations.idiomatic: "Not even a filial son's longing for his mother, or a hawk's pursuit of sparrows, could match his devotion."

sentences.zh: 若鄭之子產，魯之季文亦未加也。

translations.literal: "Even Zichan of Zheng or Jiwen of Lu would not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: "Even Zichan of Zheng or Jiwen of Lu would not surpass him."

sentences.zh: 然惡直醜正，盜憎主人。

translations.literal: "Yet the wicked hate the upright and thieves hate their master."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the wicked hate the upright, and thieves hate their master."

sentences.zh: 自往年以來，羣姦不息，劫訢宗人李英等四家，焚燒舍宅，傷害良善。

translations.literal: "Since last year bandits have not ceased; they robbed four households including Xin's clansman Li Ying, burned their dwellings, and harmed the innocent."
translations.idiomatic: "Since last year bandits have not ceased. They robbed four households including Xin's clansman Li Ying, burned their dwellings, and harmed innocent people."

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可恕！

translations.literal: "If this can be borne, what cannot be forgiven!"
translations.idiomatic: "If this can be tolerated, what outrage could not be forgiven!"

sentences.zh: 有司可明加購募，必令擒殄。」

translations.literal: "The relevant offices should clearly increase rewards for capture and ensure that the culprits are seized and destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: "The relevant offices should post clear rewards for capture and ensure that the culprits are seized and destroyed."

sentences.zh: 六月，顯袓崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Emperor Xianzu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Emperor Xianzu died.

sentences.zh: 訢遷司空，進爵范陽公。

translations.literal: Xin was transferred to Minister of Works and advanced to Duke of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was promoted to Minister of Works and raised to Duke of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 七月，以訢為侍中、鎮南大將軍、開府儀同三司、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Xin was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Guards the South, with the ceremonial trappings of the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xin was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Guards the South, with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 范𢷋知文明太后忿訢也，又知內外疾之。

translations.literal: Fan Xie knew that Empress Dowager Wenming resented Xin and also knew that inside and outside the court detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xie knew that Empress Dowager Wenming resented Xin and that he was detested throughout court and realm.

sentences.zh: 太和元年二月，希旨告訢外叛。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Taihe, to please those in power he reported that Xin was plotting rebellion abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Taihe, seeking to please those in power, he reported that Xin was plotting rebellion abroad.

sentences.zh: 文明太后徵訢至京師，言其叛狀，訢曰無之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned Xin to the capital and stated the charges of rebellion; Xin said there were none.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned Xin to the capital and confronted him with charges of rebellion. Xin denied them.

sentences.zh: 引𢷋證訢，訢言：「爾妄云知我，吾又何言！

translations.literal: Fan Xie was brought in to testify against Xin. Xin said, "You falsely claim to know me—what more can I say!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xie was brought in to testify against him. Xin said, "You falsely claim to know me—what more can I say!"

sentences.zh: 雖然，爾不顧余之厚德而忍為此，不仁甚矣。

translations.literal: "Even so, you disregard my deep kindness to you and can bear to do this—how utterly lacking in humanity!"
translations.idiomatic: "Even so, you disregard the deep kindness I showed you and can bear to do this—how utterly heartless!"

sentences.zh: 」𢷋曰：「公德於𢷋，何若李敷之德於公？

translations.literal: Fan Xie said, "Your grace to me—how does it compare with Li Fu's grace to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xie replied, "The kindness you showed me—how does it compare with the kindness Li Fu showed you?"

sentences.zh: 公昔忍於敷，𢷋今敢不忍於公乎？

translations.literal: "You once bore hard against Fu—how should I, Fan Xie, now dare not bear hard against you?"
translations.idiomatic: "You once hardened your heart against Fu—why should I now dare spare you?"

sentences.zh: 」訢慨然曰：「吾不用璞言，自貽伊戚，萬悔於心，何嗟及矣！

translations.literal: Xin said with a sigh, "I did not heed Pu's words and brought this sorrow on myself. Ten thousand regrets fill my heart—what use is lament now!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin sighed and said, "I did not heed Pu's warning and brought this ruin on myself. My heart is filled with regret—but what use is lament now!"

sentences.zh: 」遂見誅。

translations.literal: He was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon executed.

sentences.zh: 訢有三子。

translations.literal: Xin had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子邃，起家拜侍御中散、東宮門大夫。

translations.literal: His eldest son Sui, on first entering service, was appointed Attending Scribe in the Imperial Secretariat and Gate Master of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Sui began his career as Attending Scribe in the Imperial Secretariat and Gate Master of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，加平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant and given the additional rank of General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant and given the additional title of General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 先訢卒。

translations.literal: He died before Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his father.

sentences.zh: 子晴，字誨明。

translations.literal: His son Qing, courtesy name Huiming.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qing, whose courtesy name was Huiming.

sentences.zh: 逃竄，遇赦免。

translations.literal: He fled and hid, and was spared by an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He fled into hiding and was spared by an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 晴子衡，字伯琳。

translations.literal: Qing's son Heng, courtesy name Bolin.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's son Heng, whose courtesy name was Bolin.

sentences.zh: 武定中，中堅將軍、齊獻武王丞相府水曹參軍。

translations.literal: During Wuding he was General of Firm Resolve and an aide in the Water Bureau of the Chief Minister's office under the Prince of Qi, Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as General of Firm Resolve and as an aide in the Water Bureau of the Chief Minister's office under the Prince of Qi, Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 邃弟令和、令度，與訢同時死。

translations.literal: Sui's younger brothers Linghe and Lingdu died at the same time as Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's younger brothers Linghe and Lingdu were executed at the same time as Xin.

sentences.zh: 訢長兄恭，字元順。

translations.literal: Xin's elder brother Gong, courtesy name Yuanshun.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's elder brother Gong, whose courtesy name was Yuanshun.

sentences.zh: 成周太守。

translations.literal: He was Administrator of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史、容成侯，諡曰簡侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Governor of Youzhou and Marquis of Rongcheng, with the posthumous title Marquis Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously honored as Governor of Youzhou and Marquis of Rongcheng, with the posthumous title Marquis Jian.

sentences.zh: 恭弟瓘，字元衡。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Guan, courtesy name Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's younger brother Guan, whose courtesy name was Yuanheng.

sentences.zh: 營丘太守，襲父爵固安侯，平西將軍。

translations.literal: He was Administrator of Yingqiu, inherited his father's title Marquis of Gu'an, and held the rank of General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Yingqiu, inherited his father's title of Marquis of Gu'an, and held the rank of General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州刺史，諡曰康侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Governor of Yanzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: On his death he was posthumously honored as Governor of Yanzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 子長生，襲。

translations.literal: His son Changsheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changsheng inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 長生卒，子元宗襲。

translations.literal: When Changsheng died, his son Yuanzong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsheng died, his son Yuanzong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 廣平郡丞，陳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was Assistant in Guangping Commandery and Administrator of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant in Guangping Commandery and as Administrator of Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 璞字季真，性惇厚，多識人物。

translations.literal: Pu, courtesy name Jizhen, was by nature sincere and thick, and knew many men of note.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, whose courtesy name was Jizhen, was sincere and steady by nature and knew many distinguished men.

sentences.zh: 歷中書博士、侍郎、漁陽王尉眷傅、左將軍、長安副將，賜爵宜陽侯，太常卿。

translations.literal: He successively served as Doctor of the Secretariat, Attendant, tutor to Prince Yu Juan of Yuyang, General of the Left, deputy commander at Chang'an, was granted the title Marquis of Yiyang, and became Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Doctor of the Secretariat, Attendant, tutor to Prince Yu Juan of Yuyang, General of the Left, and deputy commander at Chang'an, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang, and rose to Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，年五十一，先訢卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming, at the age of fifty-one, he died before Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chengming era, at the age of fifty-one, he died before his brother Xin.

sentences.zh: 贈安西將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yongzhou, with the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 子暉，中書議郎。

translations.literal: His son Hui was a Discussion Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui served as Discussion Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 暉弟固，太學博士、高密太守。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Gu was Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Administrator of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Gu served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy and Administrator of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 固弟欽，州主簿。

translations.literal: Gu's younger brother Qin was Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's younger brother Qin served as Chief Clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 欽子奭，字元熾。

translations.literal: Qin's son Shi, courtesy name Yuanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's son Shi, whose courtesy name was Yuanchi.

sentences.zh: 武定末，鎮西將軍、南營州別駕。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was General Who Guards the West and Administrator-in-Attendance of Southern Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wuding era he served as General Who Guards the West and Administrator-in-Attendance of Southern Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 奭弟盛，字仲炎。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Sheng, courtesy name Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Sheng, whose courtesy name was Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 安東將軍、開府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was General Who Pacifies the East and Consulting Aide on the staff with the ceremonial trappings of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General Who Pacifies the East and Consulting Aide on a commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 盛弟叔樊，平西將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Sheng's younger brother Shufan was General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's younger brother Shufan served as General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 欽弟蘊，字宗令，有器幹。

translations.literal: Qin's younger brother Yun, courtesy name Zongling, had capacity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's younger brother Yun, whose courtesy name was Zongling, was a man of talent and executive ability.

sentences.zh: 中書學生、祕書中散、侍御中散。

translations.literal: He was a student of the Secretariat, Attending Scribe of the Secretariat, and Attending Scribe in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student at the Secretariat school, then Attending Scribe of the Secretariat and Attending Scribe in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為燕郡、范陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Administrator of Yan Commandery and Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to administer Yan Commandery and Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 入為員外散騎常侍、尚書右丞、中堅將軍，遷左丞。

translations.literal: He entered court as Extraordinary Regular Attendant, Vice Director of the Right in the Masters of Writing, and General of Firm Resolve, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Extraordinary Regular Attendant, Vice Director of the Right in the Masters of Writing, and General of Firm Resolve, and was later promoted to Vice Director of the Left.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年卒，贈平遠將軍、南青州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Yanchang; posthumously he was given General of Level Distance and Governor of Southern Qingzhou, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Yanchang era and was posthumously honored as General of Level Distance and Governor of Southern Qingzhou, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 初，崇之歸魏也，與州里北平田彪俱降，而彪子孫遂微劣焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chong submitted to Wei, he surrendered together with Tian Biao of Beiping, a fellow townsman; yet Biao's descendants thereafter fell into obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong first submitted to Wei, he surrendered together with Tian Biao of Beiping, a fellow townsman. Yet Biao's descendants thereafter sank into obscurity.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魏氏之有天下，百餘年中，任刑為治，蹉跌之間，便至夷滅。

translations.literal: The historian says: In the hundred-odd years that the Wei house held the realm, they governed by punishment; in a single stumble they were brought to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In the hundred-odd years that the Wei house held the realm, they governed through punishment. In a single misstep they were brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 竇瑾、李訢器識既美，時曰良幹。

translations.literal: Dou Jin and Li Xin were both gifted in talent and discernment and were called able pillars of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin and Li Xin were both men of outstanding talent and judgment, and their contemporaries called them able pillars of the state.

sentences.zh: 瑾以片言疑似，訢以夙故猜嫌，而嬰合門之戮，悲夫！

translations.literal: Jin on a few words of suspicion, Xin on long-standing grudges and suspicion—yet both suffered slaughter of the entire household. How lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell on a few words of suspected disloyalty, Xin on old grudges and suspicion—yet both brought execution upon their entire households. How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 宗之不全，自貽伊戚矣。

translations.literal: That Zongzhi did not preserve himself was a sorrow he brought upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: That Zongzhi did not preserve himself was a ruin he brought upon himself.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 為高宗博士諮議 北史卷二七李訢傳無「諮議」二字。

translations.literal: "Erudite and Consulting Aide to Emperor Gaozong": the biography of Li Xin in Northern History, juan 27, lacks the two characters "Consulting Aide."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Erudite and Consulting Aide to Emperor Gaozong": the biography of Li Xin in the Northern History, juan 27, does not include the two characters for "Consulting Aide."

sentences.zh: 按卷四九李靈傳云：「拜中書博士，選授高宗經，」亦不云為「諮議」。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Li Ling in juan 49: "He was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat and selected to instruct Emperor Gaozong in the classics," and it likewise does not say "Consulting Aide."
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Li Ling in juan 49 states, "He was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat and selected to instruct the crown prince in the classics," and likewise does not mention "Consulting Aide."

sentences.zh: 二字疑衍。

translations.literal: The two characters are suspected to be a spurious addition.
translations.idiomatic: The two characters are probably a spurious addition.
